A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
parasitoid attack is beneficial for the plant and detrimental to the herbivore, and that the parasitoid benefits from the herbivore.

The main takeaway from our work is that
parasitoid attack on herbivores may be beneficial for the plant, even when parasitism does not result in death of the herbivore.
plants that are able to attract and retain parasitoids of their herbivores may be able to reduce the negative fitness consequences of herbivory.
the plant–herbivore–parasitoid interaction is not a zero‐sum game.
